messages:
owen: After upgrading redwoodctl via the MSI installer, my `redwoodctl local serve --profile dev` now fails with a 'profile version mismatch' error. I just overwrote the previous install. Any ideas?

maria: did you see any prompt to migrate config when you updated? we shipped a profile v2 migration last quarter.

owen: No prompt. Error output: "profile version mismatch: found 1, expected 2". Snippet from %APPDATA%\Redwood\config.yaml: ```profiles:
  dev:
    version: 1
    auth_flow: device_code
```

chris: try `redwoodctl profile migrate` — there is a migration command in >=0.14. If that fails, move the old config aside and run `redwoodctl init` to recreate.

owen: `redwoodctl profile migrate` errors with `failed to parse profile: unknown field 'auth_flow'`.

kevin: Windows MSI upgrades sometimes skip the post-install hook when files are locked. Also watch out for credential helper name changes — tokens can live in Credential Manager under a different key after an upgrade. Run `cmdkey /list` to inspect, and `cmdkey /delete:<name>` to remove stale entries.

owen: I killed any running redwoodctl processes and retried migrate, same error. Logs show: ```ERROR failed to parse profile: unknown field 'auth_flow' at config.yaml:12```

maria: that field was flattened into `auth.type` in the v2 schema. You can either run the migration command (should do a transform) or do a quick manual transform. We added an import helper: `redwoodctl profile import --from-file %APPDATA%\Redwood\config.yaml --auto-upgrade` — that should auto-map old keys.

chris: if you need a quick unblock: create a fresh profile and re-login, e.g.
```
redwoodctl profile create migrated-dev
redwoodctl auth login --profile migrated-dev --browser
```
This avoids parsing the legacy file entirely.

owen: tried that but the browser flow immediately returns `401: token not found`. So it looks like the auth step completes but the CLI can't persist the new token.

kevin: yep, likely credential store collision. MSI historically wrote system-scoped credentials under a different name. Check both %APPDATA% and C:\ProgramData for leftover config files. Also check Credential Manager for entries named like `RedwoodCtlToken` vs `redwood-ctl-token`. Delete the old one and retry login.

owen: found another config copy at C:\ProgramData\Redwood\config.yaml created by the MSI. Removing that copy and re-running the login flow fixed it — `local serve` starts fine now. :raised_hands:

maria: thanks for troubleshooting. We should make the installer do a migration during upgrades and normalize the credential namespace to avoid system vs user collisions.

chris: will add an integration test covering an MSI upgrade path where an old config + old credential exists, then run migrate.

dev-bot: New issue created: GH#1234 - "msi: run profile migration on upgrade and normalize Windows credential keys". Labels: [devex, windows, installer].

kevin: also logging this in the release notes checklist so PMs know to warn Windows users about possible manual cleanup until the fix ships.

owen: confirmed fixed locally — thanks all. If someone wants the exact cleanup checklist I used I can paste it here.
maria: please do, will paste into the issue.
owen: cleanup commands I ran: ```powershell
# check credential keys
cmdkey /list | Select-String Redwood
# delete stale key (if present)
cmdkey /delete:RedwoodCtlToken
# move aside old config
move $env:APPDATA\Redwood\config.yaml $env:APPDATA\Redwood\config.yaml.bak
# re-create profile and login
redwoodctl profile create migrated-dev
redwoodctl auth login --profile migrated-dev --browser
```

maria: perfect, adding to GH#1234. :thumbsup:
